env: conda env raytun3r, python 3.11.15, matplotlib 3.11.1; unchanged from #14

sequences_available.note: No data was missing. synthetic_video.vrs and depth/depth_images.vrs are on disk for every sequence; videos_synthetic/ and depth_npy/ are decoded caches that existed only for seq131 (depth also for 5 others). 13 sequences still need depth_npy extracted as well and were left alone.

cache_naming_defect_found.rule_recovered: a stem is frame_<idx>_<ts>.png with idx the record index in the REAL video.vrs camera-rgb stream and ts that record's capture_timestamp_ns; a synthetic record takes the name of the NEAREST real record (offset +312 on seq131, residual lag 15.4 -> 0.09 ms, never half a frame)
cache_naming_defect_found.defect_1: synthetic record 0 is omitted (would be frame_000312_*)
cache_naming_defect_found.defect_2: the last record is written TWICE, as frame_003189_* and frame_003190_*, so frame_003190 carries pixels 33 ms older than its name and is scored against the wrong depth map. 1 frame in 2878 of seq131's candidate set.
cache_naming_defect_found.impact: negligible for aggregates, but it is a real mispairing in the data every ADT-FOV number so far was measured on

partA_6seq.role: the headline Part A; the three figures live here

partA_seq131.role: Part B's N=1 baseline, and seq131's entry in the per-sequence comparison

partA_seq131_200f.role: not requested by the ticket; run to verify the pooling change against fovbench-v3-24b38e1 on identical data

digest_invariant.requirement: one digest across every run in Parts A and B
digest_invariant.held_for: Part B -- all four configurations and their N=1 baseline share 8ca25fd0ebd2, so the context comparison is on identical pixels
digest_invariant.not_held_for: the 6-sequence Part A (601fcb22767e) and the five per-sequence runs, which are DIFFERENT splits by construction and are reported as such rather than folded in
digest_invariant.how_part_B_was_restricted: a one-symlink ADT root at /tmp/adt_seq131, NOT --manifest; build_split there reproduces 8ca25fd0ebd2 exactly, with and without context, because the digest is sha1(protocol + frame keys) and excludes the root path

manifest_context_bug_found.symptom: four Part B runs whose predictions were bit-identical to N=1 in all 12 cells while results.json config reported context_frames: 10
manifest_context_bug_found.cause: a manifest stores context_frames/context_stride and a pre-baked per-frame context dict; Split.load restores all of it (split.py:136-147), so --manifest silently overrides --context-frames and the run's own config block still echoes the CLI flags
manifest_context_bug_found.consequence: --manifest plus --context-frames is a silent no-op whose artifacts are indistinguishable from a real context run except by diffing against the baseline
manifest_context_bug_found.status: those four runs were discarded and re-run without --manifest; context confirmed real (0 of 12 cells identical to N=1 in every configuration)
manifest_context_bug_found.suggested_fix: refuse --context-frames that disagrees with the manifest, or rebuild the context lists from the CLI and say so in the header

pooling_verification.ticket_prediction: moves exactly one cell (DAv2 rect 0-10 deg, 0.1101 -> 0.0915), depth heads untouched
pooling_verification.measured: the named cell is exact (0.1101 -> 0.0915); depth heads untouched is exact (0 of 72 depth-head cells moved); but 8 of 96 cells moved by >0.0005, not one -- all eight are DAv2
pooling_verification.effect_on_the_dav2_anomaly: rect pen 0.733 -> 0.809 (real) and 0.727 -> 0.875 (synthetic); reduced, not removed

gpu_utilisation_note: The harness is CPU-bound, not GPU-bound: measured mid-run at 25-30% on one GPU with 3.1 GB of 48 GB resident and ~2 of 64 cores busy. Running the configurations concurrently across both GPUs reached 99-100% on both and cut the grid from ~1.4 h serial to ~28 min wall clock. Intra-run parallelism would be a change under fovbench/ and is not attempted here.
